<a name="_gjdgxs"></a><span style="font-family: Cambria, serif; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0cm; font-size: 16px;">This project introduces you to practical techniques for distinguishing between legitimate and malicious network traffic. Network operators frequently perform this task to ensure network security and detect potential threats.</span><a name="_qr9stnygi6mf"></a>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">In this project, you will analyze a <b>pcap file</b> (</span><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Roboto Mono'; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Roboto Mono'; mso-bidi-font-family: 'Roboto Mono'; color: #188038;">evaluation.pcap</span><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">) that contains network traffic from multiple hosts. This file includes a mix of <b>legitimate and malicious traffic</b>. Your task is to investigate the traffic patterns using <b>Wireshark</b> and then create <b>Snort rules</b> to automatically differentiate between benign and malicious activity.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">By completing this project, you will gain hands-on experience with:</span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">●<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Understanding and analyzing different types of network traffic.</span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">●<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Using <b>Wireshark</b> to inspect packets and detect suspicious activity.</span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">●<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Writing <b>Snort rules</b> to identify malicious traffic based on predefined attack patterns.</span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">●<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Running <b>Snort</b> to test your detection rules and generate alerts when malicious activity is found.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Through this process, you will develop a deeper understanding of <b>network security monitoring</b>, <b>intrusion detection systems (IDS)</b>, and the <b>fundamentals of network forensics</b>.</span>

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">In a DDoS, attackers usually keep making full TCP/UDP connections to the remote server. <span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; background: white; mso-highlight: white;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">In this dataset, an attacker host repeatedly initiates TCP connections to a remote access service on a victim host. Your task is to determine whether the evaluation PCAP contains a connection-attempt flood targeting FTP (TCP/21) or SSH (TCP/22).</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; background: white; mso-highlight: white;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">In addition to identifying the targeted protocol, you must capture and describe the relevant traffic behavior associated with the flood in order to receive full credit. This may include a high rate of connection attempts from the same source, repeated TCP handshakes or connection initiations, unusually short-lived or incomplete connections, repeated connection resets/terminations, and any protocol-level artifacts visible after a connection is established.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; background: white; mso-highlight: white;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; background: white; mso-highlight: white;">We do not provide a sample pcap for this category. You are expected to research and understand the differences between FTP and SSH traffic, including how brute-force attempts may manifest differently in each protocol.</span>

&nbsp;

<i><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: #2d2d2d; background: white; mso-highlight: white;">&nbsp;</span></i>

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="1" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l27 level1 lfo9;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">We consider a connection to be “<span style="color: #333333; background: #F8F8F8;">src_ip:src_port:dest_ip:dest_port</span>”. You can compare the number of DDoS/Flood/WebAttack/Botnet you got with the statistics below. If the number is close, you are likely on the right track.</span></li>
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l27 level1 lfo9;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">You can view the pcap file in Wireshark to confirm you are finding the right connections.</span></li>
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l27 level1 lfo9;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Last, you can verify your result by submitting your answer to the gradescope (See steps 4&amp;5). <li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l27 level1 lfo9;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; background: yellow; mso-highlight: yellow;">Submission limit: </span>
<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="1" type="a">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l27 level2 lfo9;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; background: yellow; mso-highlight: yellow;">You can submit <b>up to 10 times</b> on Gradescope.</span></li>
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l27 level2 lfo9;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; background: yellow; mso-highlight: yellow;">We recommend to have all your rules ready before you try out on gradescope.</span></li>
</ol>
</li>
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l27 level1 lfo9;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; background: white; mso-highlight: white;">Running a single snort rule against the evaluation.pcap can get a <span style="color: red;">different result</span> when you run it along with other snort rules.</span><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"> This is related to the limitation of Snort.<b> So please<span style="color: red;"> run all your rules together</span> to get the result we want.</b></span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<h3 style="mso-pagination: none; page-break-after: auto; margin: 14.0pt 0cm 4.0pt 0cm;"><a name="_edbe97lhew2i"></a><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-size: 13.0pt; font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: black;">Grading</span></b><b></b></h3>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Your Snort rules file will be evaluated using an autograder based on four attack categories:</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<table class="MsoNormalTable" style="border-collapse: collapse; mso-table-layout-alt: fixed; border: none; mso-yfti-tbllook: 1536; mso-padding-alt: 0cm 5.4pt 0cm 5.4pt; mso-border-insideh: cell-none; mso-border-insidev: cell-none;" border="1" width="224" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<tbody>
<tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 0; mso-yfti-firstrow: yes; height: 25.75pt;">

</tr>
<tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 1; height: 25.75pt;">

<td style="width: 71.5pt; border-top: none; border-left: none; border-bottom: solid black 1.0pt; border-right: solid black 1.0pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid black .75pt; mso-border-left-alt: solid black .75pt; mso-border-alt: solid black .75pt; padding: 5.0pt 5.0pt 5.0pt 5.0pt; height: 25.75pt;" valign="top" width="95"><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">25%</span></b></td>

<td style="width: 71.5pt; border-top: none; border-left: none; border-bottom: solid black 1.0pt; border-right: solid black 1.0pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid black .75pt; mso-border-left-alt: solid black .75pt; mso-border-alt: solid black .75pt; padding: 5.0pt 5.0pt 5.0pt 5.0pt; height: 25.75pt;" valign="top" width="95"><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">25%</span></b></td>
</tr>
<tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 3; height: 25.75pt;">
<td style="width: 96.25pt; border: solid black 1.0pt; border-top: none; mso-border-top-alt: solid black .75pt; mso-border-alt: solid black .75pt; padding: 5.0pt 5.0pt 5.0pt 5.0pt; height: 25.75pt;" valign="top" width="128"><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">WebAttack</span></b></td>
<td style="width: 71.5pt; border-top: none; border-left: none; border-bottom: solid black 1.0pt; border-right: solid black 1.0pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid black .75pt; mso-border-left-alt: solid black .75pt; mso-border-alt: solid black .75pt; padding: 5.0pt 5.0pt 5.0pt 5.0pt; height: 25.75pt;" valign="top" width="95"><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">25%</span></b></td>
</tr>
<tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 4; mso-yfti-lastrow: yes; height: 25.75pt;">
<td style="width: 96.25pt; border: solid black 1.0pt; border-top: none; mso-border-top-alt: solid black .75pt; mso-border-alt: solid black .75pt; padding: 5.0pt 5.0pt 5.0pt 5.0pt; height: 25.75pt;" valign="top" width="128"><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Botnet</span></b></td>
<td style="width: 71.5pt; border-top: none; border-left: none; border-bottom: solid black 1.0pt; border-right: solid black 1.0pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid black .75pt; mso-border-left-alt: solid black .75pt; mso-border-alt: solid black .75pt; padding: 5.0pt 5.0pt 5.0pt 5.0pt; height: 25.75pt;" valign="top" width="95"><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">25%</span></b></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">There are 4 attack categories as described above, each of which carries 25% grade weight.</span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">For each attack category, your grade = #correct alerts / (#real correct alerts + #incorrect alerts). Therefore, if you raise alerts for packets that are benign as one of the attack categories (false positives), you will lose points for that attack category. Also, if you miss raising an alert for an attack packet, you will lose points for that category. </span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">We will calculate your final grade for each category (which has 25 points as a full mark) by #final grade = min(25, #grade-for-one-category * 125%), which means if you catch <b>80% </b>of the attacks correctly, you can get full marks for the category.</span>

&nbsp;

<b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span></b>

&nbsp;

<b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-size: 12.0pt; font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Statistics for each type of unique connections (<span style="color: red;">Important</span>!)</span></b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-size: 12.0pt; font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">:</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Arial',sans-serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Arial;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Arial',sans-serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Arial; color: black; mso-color-alt: windowtext; background: #EFEFEF; mso-no-proof: yes;"><!-- [if gte vml 1]><v:shape id="image1.png" o:spid="_x0000_i1025"
 type="#_x0000_t75" style='width:510pt;height:81pt;visibility:visible;
 mso-wrap-style:square'>
 <v:imagedata src="file:///C:/Users/ADMINI~1/AppData/Local/Temp/msohtmlclip1/01/clip_image003.png"
  o:title=""/>
</v:shape><![endif]--><!-- [if !vml]--><img decoding="async" src="data:image/png;base64," width="680" height="108" border="0"><!--[endif]--></span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Arial',sans-serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Arial;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">(<u>The number might be a little different when you try to find it in Wireshark. Use the number that Snort gives you</u>)</span></b>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">We consider a connection to be “src_ip:src_port:dest_ip:dest_port”.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </span></span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Run<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </span>“<b>python3<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </span>~/count.py<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </span>alert_fast.txt</b>” to check the unique connections of your alert_fast.txt and generate the results in `connections.txt`. If your alert JSON file is generated in the home directory, you might need to add sudo in front of your command. </span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<h2 style="text-indent: 0cm; margin: 14.0pt 5.4pt .0001pt 0cm;"><a name="_v49q3h9ok8gb"></a><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">FAQs</span></h2>
&nbsp;

<h3 style="mso-pagination: none; page-break-after: auto; margin: 14.0pt 0cm 4.0pt 0cm;"><a name="_g55laznwkw7h"></a><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-size: 13.0pt; font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: black;">Getting Started</span></b></h3>
&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="1" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">This all seems too hard, how do I start?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Identify the attack from the list of possible attacks for each section. Once you have identified the attack, analyze the attack traffic packet headers (HTTP/TCP headers), and identify the common characteristics in the attack traffic. Use this information to craft your Snort rule.</span>

&nbsp;

<h3 style="mso-pagination: none; page-break-after: auto; margin: 14.0pt 0cm 4.0pt 0cm;"><a name="_o6opqpfiy09x"></a><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-size: 13.0pt; font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: black;">Rule Development &amp; Behavior</span></b></h3>
&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="2" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Why did my rule change the number of packets captured<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </span>for a particular attack when I added a rule for a different attack?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">If rules are too generic, they capture a broad range of packets leading to possible shadowing of other rules. If you do not see the output for a rule or you see that the count has changed, make sure you double check all your rules to ensure they are not too generic.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="3" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">I am not seeing the exact count for the DdoS and Bruteforce/connection attempt flood rules as listed in the writeup.</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">DdoS and Bruteforce/Flood are volumetric attacks. Thresholding can help tune out benign traffic. <b><u>You are not expected to match the numbers in the writeup for these attacks.</u></b> If you are within a ~10-15% margin of the number in the writeup(i.e. you have a rule that can successfully identify attack traffic from benign traffic), you will be awarded full points.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="4" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">What are volumetric attacks and what do I do about it?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">DdoS and Bruteforce/Flood attacks rely on a large number of requests in their attacks. These attacks generate a high volume of attack traffic. Content filtering might not be the best course of action. To identify such attacks, use the I/O graphs and threshold filters! </span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="5" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Everytime I run my rules, the number of connections identified for the Bruteforce/Flood traffic changes. Why is this?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">This is related to how Snort parses packets and is expected behavior. Therefore, we provide a margin of ~10-15%</span>

&nbsp;

<h3 style="mso-pagination: none; page-break-after: auto; margin: 14.0pt 0cm 4.0pt 0cm;"><a name="_bv1vjvbhmjau"></a><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-size: 13.0pt; font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: black;">Grading and Credit</span></b></h3>
&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="6" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Do I get partial credits if the snort rule is not 100% correct?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Partial credit is awarded according to how many false positives are detected. Please refer to the grading algorithm above.</span>

&nbsp;

<h3 style="mso-pagination: none; page-break-after: auto; margin: 14.0pt 0cm 4.0pt 0cm;"><a name="_po6f731q68p2"></a><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-size: 13.0pt; font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: black;">Tools and Resources</span></b></h3>
&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="7" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Do you provide sample pcaps for Ddos?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">No, we don’t provide sample pcaps for dos because you can observe dos from the evaluation pcap.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </span>A good start is reading some existing snort rules for detecting dos attacks to get a sense of it.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="8" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">After grading this assignment, will you release the correct answers?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">–<span style="mso-tab-count: 1;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span>No, we don’t, since similar projects run across semesters.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="9" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Should we ignore instances of ICMP and IP?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">– <span style="mso-tab-count: 1;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span>You can ignore ICMP &amp; IP</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="10" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Is Tshark/Wireshark installed on the virtual machine?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">–<span style="mso-tab-count: 1;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span>Yes. If the VM is too slow for you, I would recommend you install pcap reading tools on your local machine and use the VM only for Snort. ‘evaluation.pcap’ is a very large file so it can take some time to load. You may need to increase the amount of RAM available to the system to get it to display properly.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="11" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Looks like I can complete the assignment without using VM?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">–<span style="mso-tab-count: 1;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span>Correct, you can complete without the VM but make sure your snort file works with the version installed in the given VM. (Snort 3)</span>

&nbsp;

<h3 style="mso-pagination: none; page-break-after: auto; margin: 14.0pt 0cm 4.0pt 0cm;"><a name="_dm14a4h5cri0"></a><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-size: 13.0pt; font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: black;">Definitions and Behavior</span></b></h3>
&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="12" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">What defines a “connection”?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">–<span style="mso-tab-count: 1;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span>A “Connection” is identified by its Source Address, Destination Address, Source Port, and Destination Port.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="13" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Any hints on what we should look for when trying to identify SPAM-ing? SMTP connections?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">–<span style="mso-tab-count: 1;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span>You may want to look at packets within a certain time frame.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="14" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Can attacks be only from one or two machines or it should be from massive bot machines?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">–<span style="mso-tab-count: 1;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span>It can be from any number of machines. The exact number is not relevant.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="15" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Should we include an IPV6 connection? or only IPV4?<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </span></span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">– <span style="mso-tab-count: 1;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span>Only IPV4</span>

&nbsp;

<h3 style="mso-pagination: none; page-break-after: auto; margin: 14.0pt 0cm 4.0pt 0cm;"><a name="_t25hqfy9wkvx"></a><b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-size: 13.0pt; font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: black;">Submission and Validation</span></b></h3>
&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="16" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">We don’t need to zip the file when we submit, right?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">–<span style="mso-tab-count: 1;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span>No, you just need to submit the two files separately: rules.py and connections.txt.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="17" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Is it possible to get 100% just using rules derived from samples?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">–<span style="mso-tab-count: 1;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span>We can’t confirm or deny. 🙂 </span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">The sample pcaps are there to give you a good idea, but we don’t claim they’re representative. You should learn the pattern in the sample pcap and try to find related or similar patterns in the evaluation pcap. Always manually verify that what you find is correct.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="18" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">I am getting some json error/json decoder error</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">– <span style="mso-tab-count: 1;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span>Yes that means your json file is too big and maybe you need to put more constraints on your snort rule to generate a smaller json file. </span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="19" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">I am seeing empty alert.json file</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">delete the previous alert_fast.txt, if any</span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">delete the previous connections.txt, if any</span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">ensure each command in your file has a unique SID.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<ol style="margin-top: 0cm;" start="20" type="1">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="margin-left: 36.0pt; text-indent: -18.0pt; mso-list: l21 level1 lfo18;"><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Why am I getting many more connections than necessary in DdoS and how should I lower it?</span></li>
</ol>
&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Try using the frequency as a filter type. Remember that the direction of tracking matters (by src VS. by dst)</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<h2 style="margin-left: 0cm; text-indent: 0cm; tab-stops: 20.9pt;"><a name="_ryrwq0hkvoz6"></a><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Resources:</span></h2>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Readings on botnets behavior:</span></b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"> Please read through the following papers, to get an understanding of what a bot is, and how botnets behave. Please note that we are not asking you to implement the proposed methodologies, <i>e.g.</i> a machine learning method to detect bots.</span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">●<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><i><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">”BotHunter: Detecting Malware Infection Through IDS-Driven Dialog Correlation”</span></i><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">, Gu et. al. </span><span lang="EN-US"><a href="http://faculty.cs.tamu.edu/guofei/paper/Gu_Security07_botHunter.pdf"><span style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: #1155cc;">http://faculty.cs.tamu.edu/guofei/paper/Gu_Security07_botHunter.pdf</span></a></span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">●<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><i><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">”BotSniffer: Detecting Botnet Command and Control Channels in Network Traffic”</span></i><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">, G. Gu, J. Zhang, W. Lee, </span><span lang="EN-US"><a href="http://faculty.cs.tamu.edu/guofei/paper/Gu_NDSS08_botSniffer.pdf"><span style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: #1155cc;">http://faculty.cs.tamu.edu/guofei/paper/Gu_NDSS08_botSniffer.pdf</span></a></span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">●<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><i><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">”BotMiner: Clustering Analysis of Network Traffic for Protocol-and Structure-Independent Botnet Detection”</span></i><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">, G. Gu, R. Perdisci, J. Zhang, W. Lee, </span><span lang="EN-US"><a href="https://www.usenix.org/legacy/event/sec08/tech/full_papers/gu/gu.pdf"><span style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: #1155cc;">https://www.usenix.org/legacy/event/sec08/tech/full_papers/gu/gu.pdf</span></a></span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Getting started with WireShark</span></b>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Here is an introductory video to Wireshark so that you can get familiar with the interface: </span><span lang="EN-US"><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qTaOZrDnMzQ"><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; font-family: Roboto; mso-fareast-font-family: Roboto; mso-bidi-font-family: Roboto; color: #0b57d0;">https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qTaOZrDnMzQ</span></a></span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Snort resources:</span></b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"> Here you can find some examples of Snort rules, and some resources so that you get familiar with Snort rules. The purpose of these resources is only to get you familiar with how Snort rules look like. You are expected to write your own Snort rules.</span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-size: 12.0pt; font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US"><a href="https://usermanual.wiki/Document/snortmanual.760997111/view"><span style="font-size: 12.0pt; font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: #1155cc;">https://usermanual.wiki/Document/snortmanual.760997111/view</span></a></span>

&nbsp;

<!-- [if !supportLists]--><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-list: Ignore;">–<span style="font: 7.0pt 'Times New Roman';">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><!--[endif]--><span lang="EN-US"><a href="https://snort-org-site.s3.amazonaws.com/production/document_files/files/000/000/596/original/Rules_Writers_Guide_to_Snort_3_Rules.pdf"><span style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: #1155cc;">https://snort-org-site.s3.amazonaws.com/production/document_files/files/000/000/596/original/Rules_Writers_Guide_to_Snort_3_Rules.pdf</span></a></span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-size: 12.0pt; font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">When you google snort syntax, you should be aware that we are using snort 3 not snort 2. There are some subtle differences between Snort 2 and Snort 3 syntax. Snort 2 syntax might result in errors when you run your rules locally. </span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Example: Writing Snort rules to detect DDoS traffic:</span></b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"> This is an example to give you an idea about how we can use our understanding of an attack, and write Snort rules with potentially long shelf life, to detect this attack. Intro reading for dos: </span><span lang="EN-US"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denial-of-service_attack"><span style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: #1155cc;">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denial-of-service_attack</span></a></span><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">. Snort for DDoS: Please </span><span lang="EN-US"><a href="https://static.us.edusercontent.com/files/fl5Xf7WKOWGKzDAfPj5UeuEg"><span style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: #1155cc;">read this </span></a></span><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">to get a general idea about how Snort can be used for this purpose. Please focus on sections 3 and 4. After reading the above, one way to detect dos traffic is to monitor the rate of incoming traffic. Here is an example Snort rule based on traffic rate: </span><span lang="EN-US"><a href="http://manual-snort-org.s3-website-us-east-1.amazonaws.com/node35.html"><span style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: #1155cc;">http://manual-snort-org.s3-website-us-east-1.amazonaws.com/node35.html </span></a></span><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</span></span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">(Notice that this link is actually the snort 2 manual. However, the syntax for detection_filter is the same in snort 2 and 3. The Snort 2 manual in this case provides a better example to illustrate this filter. For other filters, especially the URL content filters, you should double check the </span><span lang="EN-US"><a href="https://usermanual.wiki/Document/snortmanual.760997111/view"><span style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: #1155cc;">snort 3 manual<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </span></span></a></span><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"><span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp;</span>and other resources online)</span>

<h2 style="text-indent: 0cm; margin: 14.0pt 5.4pt .0001pt 0cm;"><a name="_u2u8f03a4exa"></a><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria; color: red;">Important Notes</span></h2>
&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Disclaimer for background traffic</span></b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">. Please note that the traffic that is found in the evaluation pcap, and/or at the Sample pcaps is not generated by us. The dataset closely resembles realist traffic. Part of this traffic might contain inappropriate content or language. We have taken extra measures and we have performed considerable effort to filter all traffic, based on commonly used inappropriate words. We have filtered the http payload and URIs. Nevertheless, it might still be possible that some inappropriate content or words might have not been filtered entirely. In case you locate such content, we are letting you know that it is not intentional, and we are not responsible for it. Also, to complete this assignment, you do not need (nor do we ask you) to click on URLs found inside http payloads.</span>

&nbsp;

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span>

&nbsp;

<b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Additional tools are not allowed.</span></b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;"> For the assignment, you are not allowed to use any available tools, related to Snort or others. For example, you are not allowed to use Snort preprocessors that may be publicly available, pre-compiled Snort rules, detection tools. etc. <b>You are expected to write your own Snort rules.</b></span>

&nbsp;

<b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">&nbsp;</span></b>

&nbsp;

<b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">Limited support for running snort locally. </span></b><span lang="EN-US" style="font-family: 'Cambria',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: Cambria; mso-bidi-font-family: Cambria;">We have the env set up for you inside the VM. Setting up the snort 3 env on your own could be troublesome. We strongly recommend you to run snort rules inside the VM we provide (you can analyze(use wireshark) the pcap outside the VM but run the rules inside the VM). </span>

&nbsp;
